title: "Pair Programming Fixed Our Pull Request Bottlenecks"
summary: Engineering Room clip: a team replaced pull-request review with pair programming, claiming it removed PR bottlenecks, kept people in flow, spread knowledge, exposed waste, and cut production defects.

assertions.quote: You don't you don't have to spend time on P request because the way the work is already done as part of peering.
when they were finished with one full request then they just started a new branch based on that full request

verdicts.note: Stacked PRs are a common response to size limits; whether that is worse than large PRs is unmeasured.

assertions.quote: if you're pair programming then you're in flow state all the time. and and it's also like an um buffer from the outer world
someone interrupt me it takes around 15 minutes to get back into flow state
I have never seen teams learn as quickly or as effectively without bare programming as with it.
nothing builds community in the team with psychological safety and all that as actually working together

verdicts.note: Collaboration correlates with safety, but the superlative is attributed to unnamed research.

assertions.quote: when you're two people sitting on waiting this team, the first time maybe it's drinking a little coffee and it's okay

verdicts.note: Plausible social mechanism reported by one team; no independent evidence.

assertions.quote: he is showing a junior for an hour and that is not pairing
If all of these four are to create pull requests all the time for all of the small changes, the team will break down immediately

verdicts.note: Google and others sustain high deploy rates with change-based review; the claim holds only when review latency is high.

DORA says approving each individual change by an external board is impossible in the continuous paradigm, but it recommends shifting to per-change peer review by a teammate during development, so the breakdown applies to external gates, not to peer review itself.

More than 25,000 Google developers put about 20,000 changes a day through mandatory per-change review into one trunk, with median latency under 4 hours and developers confirming the process works well at scale; one highly tuned company, not a GitHub pull-request setup.

assertions.quote: on the defects side we have very few defects in production
that's much more personally rewarding even to an old introvert like me
